name: Valla

namesake.text: Lorenzo Valla, who exposed the Donation of Constantine (stated in the catalog; the job README itself states no namesake)

role: Before dossiers are assembled, Valla indexes the reasoning premises behind existing claims, flags shared premises for independent re-examination, and seals that reading context into each review packet; it never decides law or changes a claim.
inputs: explicit method and component review records
outputs: sealed context inside each claim-kit packet (PACKET.json, READ.md, view)

results.text: Published run 40987576100 (finished 2026-10-30T02:05:44Z): 612 active claims scanned, 783 shared-rationale references, 11 textual leads, 0 examined dependencies, 0 valid components, 0 model calls, 0 legal promotions. The full reasoning-dependency capability is implemented, but integrated production examined no dependencies.
PR104 native retained completion: 7 attempted, 5 changed-prior-research exceptions, 2 blocked, 0 current eligible or published; engineering accepted with retained refusals; no canonical filing.

Context-scoping repair (audit items H01-H07) on identical pinned inputs: a real completion with a concurrent publication went from 506 s and 0 filed to 122 s and 16 filed; apply 143.7 s to 8.8 s; batch-check 158.8 s to 29.3 s; 7 false invalidations removed while all 18 relevant perturbations still invalidate. These are machine-time measurements, not a research saving.

Bounded pilot: 331 active claims scanned, 11 exact span leads across 8 claims; five specific first-end assertions held through the existing exact audit-hold route (branch ready count 230 to 225); no net rework saving measured; recall and precision not estimated.

history.text: Packet context scoped to the requested instruments, per-query package bounds, once-per-invocation verification (H01-H07); later review fixes for lock placement and Windows paths.
Valla exposed an optional working_text layout cue on reviewer cards; reviewer-only normalization that keeps disclosures and original hashes was added to Mountweazel and the leak scan extended.
Repairs after merge: historical-gate replay, archived inventories, current Valla validation without renewing frozen attestations.
First build: trace exact premises and preserve explicitly reviewed preparation.

caveats: Runs BEFORE claim-kit and reads canonical claims and explicit review records, never claim-kit's generated output (no cycle): jobs/valla/README.md:17-23; jobs/claim-kit/after.txt lists valla.

A text match is a lead, not a finding: even identical normalized text establishes no legal identity, dependency or error (README.md:33-35). Three of the eleven pilot spans only say no express sunset exists and were not treated as proof of an error (pilot REPORT.md:42-48).

Valla cannot create source-audit holds; the five holds on EO 13792, 13101, 13148, 13783 and 13807 came from separate independent examination of its leads (README.md:111-114; research/readiness/SOURCE_AUDIT_HOLDS.jsonl:2-6). The 'readiness-tracker' feed is that indirect, human/agent-written route.
Integrated production examined 0 dependencies and found 0 valid components, so the new reasoning-dependency capability is unobserved at scale.
Code adoption through the main integration (PR107) is not scientific acceptance; every proposed correction still needs independent whole-case review (README.md:109-110).
Owner question A-20261029-1 (change to how packet context counts committed packages) is still listed open in HANDOFF/KEAN.md:23 at this commit.
Junto receives only an owner-seeded, unverified 'valla_rework_salvage' hypothesis; the pilot's preparation timings cannot establish rework savings (README.md:133-146).

name: Mountweazel

namesake.text: Lillian Virginia Mountweazel, the invented fountain designer planted in the 1975 New Columbia Encyclopedia to catch copiers

role: Mixes already-upheld claims with copies that carry one known planted defect, then scores whether an AI reviewer catches the planted flaws, so a reviewer's quality is measured instead of assumed.
inputs: reviewer verdicts on a blinded batch
sealed answer key held outside the repository
outputs: blinded review batch and sealed key (outside the repo)
fixtures the claim gate must reject

results.text: Experiment MW-C2: 40 real claims with 10 artifact-free plants (D3 x2, D4, D6 x3, D7 x2, D8 x2). Opus with held sources caught 8 of 10 mechanically, adjudicated down to 7 of 10 (earlier-event omission D6: 0 of 3); Opus packet-only 9 of 10; Sonnet with sources 6 of 10. One experiment, small n.
Trial MW-C1 found three seeding faults (a rationale-rewrite tell, a recurring duty mistaken for a one-time duty, a coverage-count test matching '49 Stat.'); all fixed for new batches.
Reviewer-card disclosure layout normalized without changing claim payloads; exact-copy leak scanning extended; preservation and leak regressions pass.

history.text: Normalize reviewer card disclosure layout without changing claim payloads.
Strict scoring and blinding corrections: a flag must match the affected locus and material issue; old keys report blinding as unknown.
Post-merge test fixes; first built as a work-in-progress snapshot with Llull.

caveats: Tests reviewer quality only; it is not a certification authority and changes no claim, status, codebook or human review (README.md:10).
Has no job.py on purpose, so the GitHub runner never executes it and it publishes no output folder (README.md:103); it is exercised by manual commands and by the portfolio-repair-check test suite.
Blinding is instructed, not technically enforced under one account; a harness roundtrip is not a reviewer-sensitivity result (README.md:116-117,128).
Plant wording is mechanical; the designed separate seeder agent and two plant checkers are not built (README.md:96-97).

The 7-to-9-of-10 catch rate is one October 20 experiment, not a standing measure of current review quality; the 10-of-10 planted controls in the NIRA sweep (jobs/kean/register/findings.jsonl:54) are not attributed to Mountweazel in that finding.
Track C 'upheld' means it passes the claim gate, not human certification (README.md:100).

history.text: Daily first-parent checkpoints of the ready count: 285 (10-24), 310 (10-28), 395 (10-29), 498 (10-30); 0 at the 10-17 checkpoint. Each is a separate generation; the gains were not produced by one tool.

Explicitly empty optional Opus-media matching counts as inapplicable after full evidence checks.

name: Capcom

namesake.text: Apollo Mission Control's capsule communicator, the one voice that told the crew where they stood

role: Turns each day's readiness checkpoint into the project's position on an Apollo 11 mission clock, using fixed effort weights, so progress can be tracked over time.
inputs: readiness tracker history on main (one snapshot per UTC day)
outputs: mission progress percentage and mission elapsed time

results.text: Checkpoint at 35b9a7585d: 498 ready, 11.615% effort-weighted progress, T+12.707 h, 0 human certified (previous checkpoint 2026-10-29: 395 ready, 11.07%, T+12.111 h).

history.text: Builder and frozen weights integrated while recovering branch work; original frozen weights unchanged.

caveats: Progress is a modeled effort-weighted share of open steps, not a measure of legal completion; weights are average model minutes per open step frozen on first build (build_mission_log.py:7-17).
Human certification is not counted here and stays 0 (build_mission_log.py:22-23).
Goal denominator is inconsistent in the files read: docstring says 16,239 APP-counted orders, MISSION_LOG.csv carries 16,286.
Dashboard figures are display values; the ready count comes from the tracker.

name: Revere

namesake.text: Paul Revere, the relay rider (stated in the catalog and Hamilton's report)

role: At each phase end a long-running coordinator writes a short state file and a fresh session continues from it, so no coordinator context grows huge.
inputs: coordinator's compact state file / HANDOFF notes
outputs: a fresh session continuing from the handoff

results.text: Catalog: phase handoffs in use since Oct 20. No matched before/after test of Revere's cost effect is recorded; Junto lists 0 resolved tests.
Hamilton's estimate: about 40% off an X1-like session (a coordinator at 150k instead of 421k). An estimate, not a result; Junto judged Revere to exceed the $10 test round on gross cost.

history.text: Proposed by Hamilton, then written into the continuous protocol: hand off to a fresh coordinator when context passes about 400k.

caveats: A working practice (handoff state files and HANDOFF notes), not a named program; kind 'software' is the closest available label.
The size of any saving is unmeasured; no verified saving is recorded.
The HANDOFF notes also carry owner-facing asks, which since Oct 28 must cite Kean ids (HANDOFF/README.md:20).
